title: fix(ui): keep idle chats responsive during background activity
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes idle conversations becoming sluggish while other sessions update or presence heartbeats arrive.

## User Impact

The open conversation avoids unnecessary transcript rendering during background activity. Sidebar data remains current, and selected-session changes, viewers, approvals, model controls, sharing, and recovery continue updating normally. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared session publications and fresh presence objects invalidated the whole foreground pane even when its rendered content was unchanged. Compare the session and presence facts consumed by that pane before scheduling a render, while always retaining the latest raw state and running existing reconciliation. Empty conversations still track recent sessions across the full roster.

## Evidence

A bundled Chromium test delivers real mocked Gateway events through the mounted application and verifies sidebar, header, and viewer DOM:

| Trigger | Before: conversation renders | After: conversation renders |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Three unrelated session title updates | 1, 1, 1 | 0, 0, 0 |
| Presence heartbeat | 1 | 0 |
| Selected conversation rename | 2 | 2 |
| Viewer arrival | 1 | 1 |

The test fails on the original rendering code for the unwanted renders and passes after the fix, including after integration with current main's session observation owner. The scenario takes 1.087 s; the browser suite takes 4.200 s (21.25 s including startup/build overhead).

Focused validation: 223 tests across nine files passed in 10.48 s, covering session events, pending settings, recovery, sharing, and headers. The new session-presentation file (16 cases) takes 5.95 s and the presence file (9 cases) takes 12.62 s on one worker, including imports and environment startup; test bodies account for 2% and 1% of those runs. The initial CI run exercised 52 browser files and 293 cases in its E2E shard. Type, lint, style, formatting, ownership guards, i18n, and unused-export checks were run; initial test-only type/lint findings were corrected. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

This changes render scheduling without changing appearance. The measurements above use synthetic fixtures; deployed latency has not been measured for this candidate.

The first CI run exposed two incomplete read-marker fixtures and a readiness race in the new browser regression. The fixtures now supply the required session fields without casts. The browser test explicitly holds and releases avatar identity loading before measuring idle updates; the original first-window assertion could include that startup completion. The production optimization is unchanged. The corrected browser scenario and its three neighboring suites pass (4 files / 8 tests, 24.53 s; scenario 971 ms). Read-marker, session-presentation, and presence checks pass (48 cases, 8.91 s on one worker), along with UI type and targeted lint checks. Fresh independent review of the fixture repairs is clean.


Final CI passed on `3b2fea86eaec4270d88e67f460e1c66d2d25abf9`, including all three UI unit shards and all 13 browser shards. Linux CI reproduced foreign renders `[0,0,0]`, heartbeat `0`, selected rename `2`, and viewer arrival `1`. Browser scenario/file time: 0.834 s / 0.945 s. CI unit test-body times: session presentation 0.229 s, presence 0.290 s, read markers 0.705 s (including module setup: 2.083 s, 2.071 s, and 3.107 s respectively).
